name: Robust Reasoning Processes
description: A research exploration: working notes toward reasoning processes — peer review, prediction markets, audits, LLM judge pipelines, debate protocols — that deliver trustworthy conclusions at known cost and resist corruption. Exploratory and brainstorm-heavy, not a textbook. Maintained by QURI (quantifieduncertainty.org) as part of the CAIRN project. Formalisms are graded [exact] / [standard shape] / [heuristic].
intro: Core quantities: epistemic weight (a process's likelihood-ratio profile), cost per validated bit, and the corruption cost curve (minimum adversary spend to distort output by a given amount). The central empirical project is replacing qualitative ratings with measurements of these quantities. Sibling wiki: Evaluation Engineering (https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org), on producing evaluations at scale and known cost.
